title: Telling About the Trip: The Past Tense

sections.title: Telling what you did
sections.content: A weekend trip is a story, and you tell it in the past tense. You know *voltam*, *voltunk* from Unit 24 and the definite past (*láttam a lovat*) from the same unit. You have also met the pet and farm verbs, so you can say what you fed, walked and stroked. The *-t* of *etet*, *sétáltat* and *simogat* joins the past ending: *etet + tem = etettem*.

sections.title: A day in the village
rows: On Saturday we were in the village.
We walked the dog in the forest.

items.english: On Saturday we were in a small village.
The dog ran in the forest.

sections.content: A definite object (*a lovat*) needs the definite ending even in the past: *simogatták a lovat*. With *én* the two sets look the same (*etettem*), so listen for *-ták/-ték* with *ők*. *gólya* ("stork") is new here: *láttam egy gólyát*.
